Anchor Browser is a cloudhosted browser automation platform for AI agents. It lets agents use websites much like a person would—navigating pages, filling forms, maintaining authenticated sessions, and extracting information—especially for workflows where there is no usable API.[1]

 How it works

You describe a web task in natural language or integrate through its SDK/MCP tooling. Anchor then runs managed Chromium browser instances, using deterministic automation where possible and AIdriven interaction when needed.[1]

 Typical uses

 Automating internal or thirdparty web portals without APIs
 Collecting data from web interfaces
 Completing repetitive browserbased operational workflows
 Handling authenticated, cookiedependent browser sessions
 Exposing browser tasks as callable automation endpoints[2][1]

 Positioning

It is aimed at productionscale browseragent infrastructure rather than a normal enduser web browser. Compared with conventional browserautomation services, Anchor emphasizes an AInative “perform web task” abstraction, while still supporting lowerlevel remote browser control via Chrome DevTools Protocol.[2]
